newsitem.title: FRANCE: No leak aboard derailed nuclear train in France.
newsitem.headline: No leak aboard derailed nuclear train in France.

text.p: A train carrying nuclear material was derailed in eastern France close to the border with Germany and Luxembourg on Tuesday but there was no radiation leakage, a French government official said.

A spokeswoman for the Moselle region prefect's office told Reuters by telephone from Metz: "A locomotive coming from Germany en route to Britain was derailed at Apach, near the border at Schengen. There was radioactive material aboard but there are no leaks."
A ministry spokesman said the cause of the derailment was unclear but three nuclear containers from the Lingen power station in northwestern Germany were now standing next to the rails.
"The three wagons and the locomotive are standing upright in the gravel next to the tracks. Nothing has fallen over, nothing dramatic has happened, it's just a derailment," the spokesman said.
The wagons were standing 500 metres (yards) inside the French border near the town of Apac, he said, adding that the French police had made clear that the containers were now their responsibility.
The remainder of the train became separated from the containers and remained on German territory, he said.
